goal.text: beat the TV projection by at least 3 runs of average miss, on the latest calendar year, which nothing was trained or chosen on.
goal.lead: At 10 overs, the TV shows a projected score. The agent tries to beat it: predict the final total, and miss by 3 runs less on average.

methods.name: the know-nothing guess
methods.note: always the training years' average final total, whatever the score at 10 overs

methods.name: the TV projection
methods.note: the broadcaster's projected score: current run rate x 20 overs

methods.name: the language model's model
methods.note: a straight line fitted on the features the language model picked

methods.name: forward selection's model
methods.note: a straight line fitted on the features forward selection picked

know_nothing.bias: leans neither way on average (0.0 runs)

sentences.headline: Here is how well two simple guesses did against the real final totals in past seasons (2005 to 2022, 2,133 innings). This is the bar the agent has to clear.
sentences.gap: The TV projection misses by 22.5 runs on average, against 23.9 for the know-nothing guess, which ignores the score at 10 overs. Knowing the score at 10 overs is worth 1.4 runs (5.9%), and 0.4 more innings in every 100 land within 10 runs.
sentences.finding: The TV projection is only slightly better than knowing nothing: its average miss is just 1.4 runs (5.9%) lower, so beating it means little.
sentences.bias: The TV projection guesses 14.3 runs too low on average, because sides tend to score faster in the last 10 overs than their run rate at the halfway mark.

meter.caption: Average miss, runs · 2005 to 2022, 2,133 innings
meter.text: Average miss, lower is better: the know-nothing guess 23.9, the TV projection 22.5, the goal 19.5 or less.

hero.caption: A real innings: Australia v India, Sydney Cricket Ground, December 2020. The first 10 overs, in grey, are context; the white part is what everyone is trying to predict. Australia went from 82/2 to 186. The TV's straight line said 164 and was 22 runs short: about its typical miss. Open circles mark wickets.
hero.panel: Knowing the score at 10 overs barely helps the TV, and on average it guesses too low, by 14.3 runs. The agent has to beat it by at least 3 runs.
hero.footnote: 2,133 past innings, 2005 to 2022: IPL, BBL and full-member internationals.
hero.chart_text: Runs by over for Australia v India, Sydney Cricket Ground, December 2020. The first 10 overs are shown in grey as context and the last 10 in the prediction area. Australia were 82 for 2 after 10 overs. The TV projection said 164. The know-nothing guess said 162. The innings finished on 186. A zoom on the finish shows where each prediction landed at 20 overs: the actual total 186, the TV projection 164 (22 runs short) and the know-nothing guess 162. The TV's usual miss is 22.5 runs either way, shown as a band around its projection. The agent's prediction is not known.
